rv.q: The Royal Exchange’s new production is the third major revival of Mike Leigh’s play in less than 12 months, after outings with Theatre Royal Stratford East and English Touring Theatre . Natalie Abrahami ’s version relocates the play to Manchester, though this could be a middle-class cul-de-sac anywhere.
Imaginatively staged revival of Mike Leigh’s 1970s comedy classic

This darkly funny production still revels in the absurd and shines a harsh spotlight on suburban life in the aspirational ’70s. Director Natalie Abrahami and set designer Peter Butler do a great job of ensuring the audience are like flies on the wall glued to every awkward move by the party guests.
A stylish, entertaining production with strong performances, though the plot twist lacks impact...
